title.en: One seller, and a tax on its price (Q2)
title.zh: 一家独大，再收一道税（第 2 题）

description.en: Where market power comes from, monopoly from MR = MC, its deadweight loss, how a tax tilts or shifts the demand the seller sees, and who really pays.
description.zh: 市场势力从哪来，用 MR = MC 解垄断，垄断的无谓损失，税怎样转动或平移卖方看到的需求，以及税到底谁付。

description.en: Reading the monopoly price off the MR curve instead of the demand curve
description.zh: 从 MR 曲线而不是需求曲线读垄断价格

description.en: Assuming the buyers pay the whole tax because it is added to their price
description.zh: 以为税加在买方价格上，就全由买方付

rows.en: $Q = 100$; the seller gets $320$, buyers pay $400$; profit $21{,}000$
tax $80$ per unit: buyers $+16$, the monopolist $-64$, so the monopolist pays 80%; government $+8{,}000$

items.en: Marginal revenue: why it is below the price for a single seller.
items.zh: 边际收益：为什么对独家卖方来说它低于价格。

items.en: $MR = MC$ for the quantity; the demand curve for the price.
items.zh: 用 $MR = MC$ 定数量；用需求曲线定价格。

items.en: A tax changes the demand the seller sees: a percentage tax rotates it, a per-unit tax shifts it.
items.zh: 税会改变卖方看到的需求：百分比税让它转动，从量税让它平移。

items.en: Incidence: who pays a tax is decided by how far each price moves, not by who hands over the money.
items.zh: 税负归宿：税由谁付，看两边价格各动了多少，不看钱是谁交的。

text.en: A monopolist is the only seller of a good with no close substitute, protected by a **barrier to entry**: otherwise its profit would attract rivals (the previous lesson). The usual barriers:
text.zh: 垄断者是某种没有相近替代品的商品的唯一卖家，并且有**进入壁垒**（barrier to entry）保护：否则它的利润会引来对手（上一课）。常见的壁垒：

items.en: **Legal**: patents, copyrights, licences, a state franchise.
items.zh: **法律**：专利、版权、执照、政府特许经营。

items.en: **Economies of scale**: one firm can supply the whole market more cheaply than two (a **natural monopoly**: water pipes, power grids).
items.zh: **规模经济**：一家厂商供应整个市场比两家更便宜（**自然垄断**：自来水管网、电网）。

items.en: **Control of a key input**, or **network effects** (a platform worth more the more people use it).
items.zh: **控制关键投入品**，或者**网络效应**（用的人越多越值钱的平台）。

text.en: Unlike a competitive firm, the monopolist faces the whole downward-sloping demand curve, so it chooses the price (or, equivalently, the quantity).
text.zh: 和竞争厂商不同，垄断者面对的是整条向下倾斜的需求曲线，所以它可以定价格（等价地说，定数量）。

title.en: Why a monopolist stops before p = MC
title.zh: 为什么垄断者在 p = MC 之前就停

text.en: To sell one more unit, a monopolist must lower the price on **every** unit it sells. So the revenue from one more unit is the price, minus what is lost on all the others:
text.zh: 想多卖一个，垄断者得把**所有**单位的价格都降下来。所以多卖一个带来的收入 = 这个单位的价格 − 其他所有单位少收的钱：

items.en: For a straight inverse demand $p = a - bQ$: $MR = a - 2bQ$, the same intercept with twice the slope.
items.zh: 直线反需求 $p = a - bQ$ 时：$MR = a - 2bQ$，截距相同，斜率翻倍。

items.en: Profit $\pi = pQ - C(Q)$ is highest where $MR = MC$. That gives $Q$; then read the price off the **demand** curve, not off $MR$.
items.zh: 利润 $\pi = pQ - C(Q)$ 在 $MR = MC$ 处最大。由此得 $Q$；价格再从**需求**曲线上读，不是从 $MR$ 上读。

items.en: Since $MC > 0$, $MR > 0$, so $|\varepsilon| > 1$: a monopolist always prices where demand is **elastic**. The markup follows the **Lerner rule**: $\frac{p - MC}{p} = \frac{1}{|\varepsilon|}$.
items.zh: 因为 $MC > 0$，所以 $MR > 0$，即 $|\varepsilon| > 1$：垄断者总在需求**富有弹性**的地方定价。加价幅度由**勒纳法则**（Lerner rule）决定：$\frac{p - MC}{p} = \frac{1}{|\varepsilon|}$。

alt.en: Demand p = 600 − 2Q, marginal revenue MR = 600 − 4Q and marginal cost MC = 60 + Q. MR meets MC at Q = 108, where MR = MC = 168; the price read off demand above it is 384. Demand meets MC at Q = 180, p = 240; the shaded triangle between Q = 108 and 180 is the deadweight loss.
alt.zh: 需求 p = 600 − 2Q、边际收益 MR = 600 − 4Q、边际成本 MC = 60 + Q。MR 与 MC 交于 Q = 108，此处 MR = MC = 168；正上方需求曲线给出价格 384。需求与 MC 交于 Q = 180、p = 240；Q 在 108 到 180 之间的阴影三角形是无谓损失。

caption.en: Find $Q$ where $MR$ meets $MC$, then go **up** to the demand curve for the price. The shaded triangle is what the monopoly costs society.
caption.zh: 在 $MR$ 与 $MC$ 的交点找 $Q$，再**往上**到需求曲线读价格。阴影三角形是垄断让社会损失的部分。

text.en: What the monopoly costs: deadweight loss

A competitive market would go on to $Q = 180$, where demand meets $MC$ ($600 - 2Q = 60 + Q$, $p = 240$). The units from 108 to 180 are worth more to buyers than they cost to make, but the monopolist does not sell them, because selling them would lower its price on all the others. The lost surplus is the triangle $\tfrac12 \times (384 - 168) \times (180 - 108) = 7{,}776$. This is why governments regulate monopolies (for example a price cap at $p = 240$, which makes the monopolist produce 180).
text.zh: 竞争市场会一直做到 $Q = 180$，即需求等于 $MC$ 处（$600 - 2Q = 60 + Q$，$p = 240$）。108 到 180 之间的那些单位，买方心里的价值高于生产成本，垄断者却不卖，因为多卖会压低其余所有单位的价格。损失的剩余是三角形 $\tfrac12 \times (384 - 168) \times (180 - 108) = 7{,}776$。这就是政府管制垄断的原因（比如把价格上限定在 $p = 240$，垄断者就会生产 180）。

why.zh: 反需求：从 $Q = 300 - \tfrac12 p$ 解出 $p$。
利润 = 收入 − 成本。

items.en: Lerner: $\varepsilon = -\tfrac12 \times \tfrac{384}{108} \approx -1.78$, and $\tfrac{384 - 168}{384} = 0.5625 = \tfrac{1}{1.78}$: elastic, as it must be.
items.zh: 勒纳：$\varepsilon = -\tfrac12 \times \tfrac{384}{108} \approx -1.78$，而 $\tfrac{384 - 168}{384} = 0.5625 = \tfrac{1}{1.78}$：富有弹性，本该如此。

prompt.en: The monopolist produces 108. Someone writes the price as 168. What went wrong?
prompt.zh: 垄断者生产 108。有人把价格写成 168。错在哪？

label.en: 168 is marginal revenue (= MC) at 108; the price is on the demand curve: 384
label.zh: 168 是 108 处的边际收益（= MC）；价格要在需求曲线上读：384

label.en: Nothing: at the optimum the price equals marginal cost
label.zh: 没错：最优点处价格等于边际成本

feedback.en: That is a competitive firm. A monopolist's price is above its marginal cost: here 384 against 168.
feedback.zh: 那是竞争厂商。垄断者的价格高于边际成本：这里是 384 对 168。

label.en: The price should be 240, where demand meets MC
label.zh: 价格应该是 240，即需求与 MC 相交处

feedback.en: 240 is the competitive price. The monopolist sells fewer units at a higher price.
feedback.zh: 240 是竞争价格。垄断者卖得更少、价格更高。

explain.en: $MR = MC$ gives the quantity. Buyers then pay what the demand curve says they will pay for 108 units: $600 - 2 \times 108 = 384$.
explain.zh: $MR = MC$ 给出数量。买家付的是需求曲线上 108 个单位对应的价格：$600 - 2 \times 108 = 384$。

title.en: A tax tilts, or shifts, the demand the seller sees
title.zh: 税会“转动”或“平移”卖方看到的需求

text.en: Buyers pay $1.25p$ when the seller gets $p$. Put the buyers' price into demand: $Q = 300 - \tfrac12(1.25p)$, so the seller faces
text.zh: 卖方收 $p$ 时，买方付 $1.25p$。把买方价格代进需求：$Q = 300 - \tfrac12(1.25p)$，于是卖方面对的是

text.en: Every point of demand is scaled down by the factor $1/1.25 = 0.8$: the curve **rotates** down around the quantity axis. A per-unit tax $t$ (the one usually done in class) instead **shifts** it down in parallel: $p = 600 - 2Q - t$. Either way, redo $MR = MC$ with the curve the seller actually faces.
text.zh: 需求上每一点都乘以 $1/1.25 = 0.8$：曲线绕数量轴往下**转**。课上常做的从量税 $t$ 则是往下**平移**：$p = 600 - 2Q - t$。不管哪种，都用卖方真正面对的曲线重做 $MR = MC$。

caption.en: Drag the tax and switch its kind. Dashed: what the seller keeps. Purple: the seller's marginal revenue. The thick bar at the chosen quantity is the tax per unit: blue above the old price 384 is paid by buyers, orange below it by the monopolist. The same slider position is the same 80 per unit at $\tau = 25\%$.
caption.zh: 拖动税率，切换税的种类。虚线：卖方实得。紫线：卖方的边际收益。所选数量处的粗竖条就是每单位税：旧价格 384 之上的蓝色部分由买方承担，之下的橙色部分由垄断者承担。滑块在同一位置时，两种税在 $\tau = 25\%$ 处都是每单位 80。

title.en: Q2b: the monopolist with the 25% tax

why.en: $MR = MC$. Cost is unchanged by the tax.
The seller gets 320; buyers pay 400 (check: $600 - 2 \times 100 = 400$ on the original demand).

prompt.en: Solve $MR = MC$ with the tax: $480 - 3.2Q = 60 + Q$.

title.en: Q2c: who pays, and what the government gets

why.en: The tax per unit is the gap between the buyers' price $p_b$ and the seller's price $p_s$ (25% of 320).
why.zh: 每单位税就是买方价格 $p_b$ 与卖方价格 $p_s$ 之差（320 的 25%）。

why.en: Buyers pay 16 more than before the tax.
The monopolist bears 80% of the tax: it pays more of it.
why.zh: 垄断者承担了 80% 的税：大部分是它付的。

why.en: Government finances improve by 8,000 (there was no tax before).
why.zh: 政府财政改善 8,000（原来没有税）。

prompt.en: How much more do buyers pay per unit than before the tax?
prompt.zh: 买方每单位比税前多付多少？

text.en: By prices (16 against 64) or by losses (1,664 against 8,160), the answer is the same: the monopolist bears most of it. The 1,824 lost by everyone is the deadweight loss of the tax: the 8 units between 100 and 108 that were worth more to buyers than they cost to make.
text.zh: 按价格（16 对 64）还是按损失（1,664 对 8,160）看，结论一样：大头由垄断者承担。所有人一起少了的 1,824 是这道税的无谓损失：100 到 108 之间那 8 个单位，买方心里的价值高于生产成本，却不再生产了。

title.en: Who pays a tax, in any market

items.en: **The rule of incidence**: the side that can less easily walk away pays more. In a competitive market the buyers' share is $\frac{\varepsilon_s}{\varepsilon_s - \varepsilon_d}$ (supply elasticity over the gap between the two elasticities): inelastic buyers pay most; with flat supply (Q5) buyers pay all of it.
items.zh: **税负归宿规则**：越不容易走开的一方付得越多。竞争市场里买方承担的份额是 $\frac{\varepsilon_s}{\varepsilon_s - \varepsilon_d}$（供给弹性除以两个弹性之差）：买方缺乏弹性时付大头；供给是水平线（第 5 题）时买方全付。

items.en: **It does not matter who hands the money over.** A tax collected from sellers or from buyers ends with the same prices and the same shares.
items.zh: **钱是谁交的不重要。** 向卖方收还是向买方收，最后的价格和分担比例都一样。

items.en: **A monopolist** re-solves $MR = MC$; the buyers' share depends on the slopes of demand and $MC$ and on the kind of tax. Here a percentage tax put 20% on buyers, the same 80 per unit as a per-unit tax would put 40% on them (try it in the figure).
items.zh: **垄断者**会重解 $MR = MC$；买方份额取决于需求和 $MC$ 的斜率，以及税的种类。这里百分比税让买方承担 20%，同样每单位 80 的从量税会让买方承担 40%（在上面的图里试试）。

items.en: **A lump-sum tax or a tax on profit** changes neither $MR$ nor $MC$, so the monopolist keeps the same $Q$ and $p$; it just earns less. No deadweight loss.
items.zh: **定额税或利润税**既不改变 $MR$ 也不改变 $MC$，垄断者的 $Q$ 和 $p$ 都不变，只是赚得少了。没有无谓损失。

summary.en: Beyond the exam: here a percentage tax beats a per-unit tax
summary.zh: 超出考试：这里百分比税比从量税好

text.en: Charge the same 80 as a per-unit tax: the seller faces $p = 520 - 2Q$, $MR = 520 - 4Q = 60 + Q$, so $Q = 92$ and revenue is $80 \times 92 = 7{,}360$. The percentage tax raised more (8,000) **and** kept more output (100). A percentage tax lowers the seller's marginal revenue less where its price is low, so it distorts a monopolist's output less.
text.zh: 换成每单位 80 的从量税：卖方面对 $p = 520 - 2Q$，$MR = 520 - 4Q = 60 + Q$，得 $Q = 92$，税收 $80 \times 92 = 7{,}360$。百分比税收得更多（8,000），**而且**保住了更多产量（100）。百分比税在卖方价格低的地方压低边际收益更少，所以对垄断产量的扭曲更小。

items.en: Using the buyers' price (400) in the profit. The monopolist only keeps 320.
items.zh: 用买方价格（400）算利润。垄断者只拿到 320。

items.en: Substituting $p - 0.25$ or $p + 25$ for the percentage tax. It multiplies: $1.25p$.
items.zh: 把百分比税写成 $p - 0.25$ 或 $p + 25$。它是乘法：$1.25p$。

items.en: Assuming buyers pay the tax because it is "added to their price". Incidence is decided by how far each price moves.
items.zh: 以为税“加在买方价格上”就由买方付。归宿看的是两边价格各动了多少。

prompt.en: A monopolist has $MC = 20 + 2Q$ and buyers' demand $p = 200 - Q$. The government adds a 20% tax: buyers pay $1.2p$ when the seller gets $p$. What output does the monopolist choose?
prompt.zh: 垄断者 $MC = 20 + 2Q$，买方需求 $p = 200 - Q$。政府加征 20% 的税：卖方收 $p$ 时买方付 $1.2p$。垄断者选多少产量？

explain.en: The seller faces $p = (200 - Q)/1.2$, so $MR = (200 - 2Q)/1.2$. Setting $MR = 20 + 2Q$: $200 - 2Q = 24 + 2.4Q$, so $Q = 40$. The seller gets $160/1.2 \approx 133.33$ and buyers pay 160.

hints.en: Write the demand the seller sees: divide the buyers' price by 1.2.
hints.zh: 写出卖方看到的需求：把买方价格除以 1.2。

prompt.en: In the same market, without the tax the monopolist sells 45 at $p = 155$. What percentage of the tax do buyers bear?
prompt.zh: 同一个市场，没有税时垄断者以 $p = 155$ 卖 45 个。买方承担了这道税的百分之几？

explain.en: Tax per unit $= 160 - 133.33 = 26.67$. Buyers' price rose $160 - 155 = 5$; $5/26.67 = 18.75\%$. The monopolist bears the other 81.25%.

title.en: Your turn: the cost of a monopoly

prompt.en: Demand is $p = 100 - Q$ and marginal cost is constant at 20. What is the deadweight loss of the monopoly, compared with competition?
prompt.zh: 需求 $p = 100 - Q$，边际成本恒为 20。和竞争相比，垄断的无谓损失是多少？

hints.en: The triangle between demand and $MC$, from the monopoly quantity to the competitive one.
hints.zh: 需求与 $MC$ 之间、从垄断数量到竞争数量的那个三角形。
